summary: This is GitHub issue #588 in the ros2/launch repository, opened by mjeronimo on Jan 24, 2022, reporting that changing the 'output' substitution type breaks dictionary usage for Node outputs. The reporter's launch file set output to a dict with stdout and stderr set to 'screen', which raised an error that 'stdoutstderr' is not a valid standard output config. The issue was fixed by pull request #640 (merged Aug 2022, cherry-picked to Humble as #647), and downstream projects referenced it for workarounds, though a later commenter reported it was still unfixed in the Humble release.
one_line: GitHub issue in ros2/launch where the 'output' option rejected dictionary values for ROS 2 nodes, fixed by PR #640 in 2022.
key_facts: GitHub issue #588 in the ros2/launch repository was titled "Changing 'output' substitution type breaks dictionary usage".
The issue was opened by mjeronimo on Jan 24, 2022 and was closed as completed on Aug 20, 2022.
The reporter used Ubuntu 20.04 with installation type source and version commit hash 8006dfa.
The reproduction launch file set output to a dictionary with 'stdout': 'screen' and 'stderr': 'screen' for a demo_nodes_cpp talker node.
The reported error was: stdoutstderr is not a valid standard output config i.e. "screen", "log" or "both".
The issue was labeled bug and help wanted.
hidmic stated on Jan 26, 2022 that a follow-up PR to support both substitutions and dictionaries would be best and most welcome, and that a regression test was also needed.
m-elwin opened pull request #640 on Aug 9, 2022 to allow a dict for 'output'.
Pull request #640 was merged and commit edf6891 said it addressed issue #588, allowing dict for 'output'.
The commit message stated that issue #577 had caused the 'output' option not to participate in $(var) expansion, and that the fix for it broke the dictionary use-case.
The fix checks whether the output value is a dict and only performs command expansion when it is not.
On Sep 27, 2022, FranekStark reported the issue was still not fixed in the current Humble release.
Several Universal Robots ROS2 driver and cartesian_controllers commits referenced this issue as a workaround for dictionary output.
